title: Occelli 2010 · sound complexity and dynamic capture
citation: Occelli, V., Spence, C., & Zampini, M. (2010). Assessing the effect of sound complexity on the audiotactile cross-modal dynamic capture task. Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, 63(4), 694–704.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

conditions.auditory_target: Discriminate the direction of the two-pulse auditory stream and ignore the tactile stream.
conditions.tactile_target: Discriminate the direction of the two-pulse tactile stream and ignore the auditory stream.
conditions.order: Counterbalance target modality; run both sound types in separate blocks within each modality.

published_method.geometry: Two physical sources 15 cm left and right of midline, roughly 50 cm from the body, paired with tactors next to the corresponding index fingers.
published_method.response: Release the pedal corresponding to the perceived target direction, prioritizing accuracy. The pedal-mapping details are described in the companion thesis, Experiment 6 (p. 171). Analyze target-direction accuracy separately by attended modality.

value.timing_gap: The paper names a 100 ms ISI. The event file or onset measurements are unavailable.

source_provenance.source: Occelli, Spence and Zampini 2010, final QJEP issue, pp. 697–698, Method, Procedure and Fig. 1
source_provenance.gap: Exact audio files, gain and sample rate remain unreported.

trajectory_count.source: Occelli doctoral thesis Experiment 6, printed pp. 169–171, Fig. 8

value.tactors: Directly in front of the paired speakers
value.hand_contact: Matching left and right index fingertips

trajectory_path.source: Occelli doctoral thesis Experiment 6, printed pp. 169–170, Fig. 8

stimulus_duration.source: Occelli, Spence and Zampini 2010, final QJEP issue, pp. 697–698, Method, Procedure and Fig. 1
stimulus_duration.gap: The paper names a 100 ms ISI. The event file or onset measurements are unavailable.

stimulus_speed.source: Occelli et al. 2010, Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology pp. 697–698, Apparatus, materials, design, and procedure
stimulus_speed.gap: Apparent motion uses successive presentations from two fixed sources 30 cm apart. There is no continuous physical movement speed.

gain_envelope.source: Occelli et al. 2010, Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology pp. 697–698, Apparatus, materials, design, and procedure
gain_envelope.gap: The article reports 82 dB(A) at the head for the stimulus pulses and a separate 75 dB masker. The pulse amplitude envelope and ramps are unreported.

tactors.placement: Immediately in front of matching task loudspeaker on 3 cm foam

value.response: One pedal beneath the toes of each foot
value.control: E-Prime via computer parallel port and custom relay
value.environment: Dim room, participants blindfolded and instructed to keep the head still facing forward

renderer_or_apparatus.source: Occelli, Spence and Zampini 2010, final QJEP issue, pp. 697–698, Method, Procedure and Fig. 1
renderer_or_apparatus.gap: E-Prime version and measured system delays unreported.

condition_intermixing.source: Occelli doctoral thesis Experiment 6, printed pp. 170–172
condition_intermixing.gap: Exact ordering, per-cell quotas, and journal-version equivalence remain unverified.

value.target_modality_order: Half started with tactile targets and half with auditory targets

blocked_or_random_order.source: Occelli doctoral thesis Experiment 6, printed p. 170
blocked_or_random_order.gap: The thesis reports counterbalancing across target modalities. The exact ordering of sound-type blocks and journal-version equivalence remain unverified.

iti_jitter_policy.source: Occelli doctoral thesis Experiment 6, printed p. 171
iti_jitter_policy.gap: Sampling probabilities and journal-version equivalence remain unverified.

response_window.source: Occelli, Spence and Zampini 2010, final QJEP issue, pp. 697–698, Method, Procedure and Fig. 1
response_window.gap: Response gate is reported. The upper response limit is not stated.

task_sequence_rules.value: Report the auditory direction by releasing the corresponding footpedal and ignore the other modality.
task_sequence_rules.source: Occelli doctoral thesis Experiment 6, printed p. 171
task_sequence_rules.gap: The journal abstract confirms the task instruction. The pedal mapping comes from the thesis.

value.file_description: Methods say the sound file also activated the tactors. Discussion says vibrotactile properties were held constant.
value.waveform_gap: The exact tactile source file and whether its spectrum varied across audio blocks remain unresolved.
value.range_scope: Manufacturer specification in Method footnote 1. Actual delivered tactile spectrum is unknown.

tactile_stimulus.source: Occelli, Spence and Zampini 2010, final QJEP issue, pp. 697–698, Method, Procedure and Fig. 1
tactile_stimulus.gap: The exact tactile source file and whether its spectrum varied across audio blocks remain unresolved.

soa_table.source: Occelli, Spence and Zampini 2010, final QJEP issue, pp. 697–698, Method, Procedure and Fig. 1

baseline_strategy.source: Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology pp. 697–698, Method, Procedure and Fig. 1

baseline_timing.source: Occelli et al. 2010, Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology pp. 697–698, Apparatus, materials, design, and procedure
baseline_timing.gap: The directional-discrimination test compares paired streams. The 12 target-only trials are a separate practice block.

catch_trial_type.source: Occelli et al. 2010, Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology pp. 697–698, Apparatus, materials, design, and procedure
catch_trial_type.gap: Methods describe paired target and distractor test streams and separate unimodal practice. No catch or no-go family is described.

repetitions_per_tactile_soa_condition.source: Occelli et al. 2010, Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology pp. 697–698, Apparatus, materials, design, and procedure
repetitions_per_tactile_soa_condition.gap: The 96-trial block total and synchronous or 500 ms delayed stream conditions are reported. The exact number at each synchrony, congruency, direction and frequency combination is unreported.

baseline_count.source: Occelli et al. 2010, Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology pp. 697–698, Apparatus, materials, design, and procedure
baseline_count.gap: The tested conditions compare paired streams. The separate 12-trial unimodal block per session is practice and is excluded from the test baseline count.

catch_count.source: Occelli et al. 2010, Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology pp. 697–698, Apparatus, materials, design, and procedure
catch_count.gap: The 96-trial block total is reported. The article gives no catch quota.

block_count.source: Occelli doctoral thesis Experiment 6, printed pp. 170–171

value.derivation: Two modalities × two blocks per modality × 96 test trials per block

total_trial_count.source: Occelli doctoral thesis Experiment 6, printed pp. 170–171

implementation_gaps: Requires separate left/right audio and tactile outputs, support for two pulses per target and distractor stream, a two-pedal release response and continuous calibrated masking audio. The usual single tactile target and single response do not express this experiment.

Verify the printed 100 ms interstimulus interval against original event files (onset-to-onset versus silent gap), the delivered tactile waveform, triggered timing, sound assets and full allocation before research execution.
reference_parameters.planner_scope: The study settings describe the source procedure. The Planner contains no executable trial schedule for this profile.
